questions.text:
Ravi had _____________ younger brother who taught at _____________ university. He was widely regarded as _____________ honorable man.
Select the option with the correct sequence of articles to fill in the blanks.
questions.solution:
"Younger brother" and "honorable man" are both non-specific, first-mention nouns (indefinite), so they take the indefinite article "a"/"an" (chosen by the following sound: "a" before a consonant sound in "younger," "an" before the vowel sound in "honorable," since the "h" is silent). "University," despite starting with a vowel letter, starts with a consonant sound ("yoo-niversity"), so it takes "a," not "an."

So the sequence is: a (younger brother), a (university), an (honorable man).

Answer: a; a; an

questions.text:
The CEO's decision to downsize the workforce was considered myopic because it sacrificed long-term stability to accommodate short-term gains.
Select the most appropriate option that can replace the word "myopic" without changing the meaning of the sentence.
questions.solution:
"Myopic" literally means near-sighted, and figuratively means lacking foresight or focused only on the short term — exactly matching "shortsighted." "Visionary," "progressive," and "innovative" all carry positive, forward-looking connotations that are the opposite of what "myopic" implies here.

Answer: shortsighted

questions.text: The average marks obtained by a class in an examination were calculated as 30.8. However, while checking the marks entered, the teacher found that the marks of one student were entered incorrectly as 24 instead of 42. After correcting the marks, the average becomes 31.4. How many students does the class have?
questions.solution:
Let the class have [latex]n[/latex] students. The total marks initially (with the error) [latex]=30.8n[/latex]. Correcting one student's mark from [latex]24[/latex] to [latex]42[/latex] adds [latex]42-24=18[/latex] to the total:

[latex]30.8n+18=31.4n\ \Rightarrow\ 18=0.6n\ \Rightarrow\ n=30[/latex]

Answer: 30

questions.text:
Consider the relationships among P, Q, R, S, and T:

P is the brother of Q.
S is the daughter of Q.
T is the sister of S.
R is the mother of Q.

The following statements are made based on the relationships given above.

R is the grandmother of S.
P is the uncle of S and T.
R has only one son.
Q has only one daughter.

Which one of the following options is correct?
questions.solution:
From the given facts: [latex]P[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s brother; [latex]S[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s daughter; [latex]T[/latex] is [latex]S[/latex]'s sister (so [latex]T[/latex] is also [latex]Q[/latex]'s daughter); [latex]R[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s mother.

- "R is the grandmother of S": since [latex]R[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s mother and [latex]S[/latex] is [latex]Q[/latex]'s daughter, [latex]R[/latex] is indeed [latex]S[/latex]'s grandmother. True.
- "P is the uncle of S and T": [latex]P[/latex], as [latex]Q[/latex]'s sibling, is uncle to [latex]Q[/latex]'s children [latex]S[/latex] and [latex]T[/latex]. True.
- "R has only one son": we're only told [latex]P[/latex] is a brother of [latex]Q[/latex] — nothing rules out [latex]R[/latex] having other sons not mentioned. Not established, so not necessarily true.
- "Q has only one daughter": we're explicitly told about two daughters of [latex]Q[/latex] ([latex]S[/latex] and her sister [latex]T[/latex]), directly contradicting this. False.

Answer: Both (1) and (2) are true.

questions.text:
According to the map shown in the figure, which one of the following statements is correct?
Note: The figure shown is representative.
questions.solution:
Using the given map layout (Library and Physics Lab on the upper-left; Canteen and Hospital on the upper-right; Hostels and Classrooms on the lower-left; Chemistry Lab on the lower-right; with North pointing up):

The Physics Lab sits in the upper-left region, while the Chemistry Lab sits in the lower-right region — directly diagonally opposite, i.e. to the southeast of the Physics Lab.

The other options don't hold up against the actual layout: the library isn't northwest of the canteen (they're roughly at the same latitude, on opposite sides), the hospital isn't east of the chemistry lab (it's north of it), and classrooms/canteen are diagonally placed, not adjacent.

Answer: The chemistry lab is to the southeast of the physics lab.
